newsitem.title: USA: NYC seeks to tap Washington's savings on Medicaid.
newsitem.headline: NYC seeks to tap Washington's savings on Medicaid.

text.p: Rosa Gil, the new chairwoman of the Health and Hospitals Corp (HHC), on Monday proposed a community health partnership that would be funded with federal Medicaid savings generated by more use of managed care.

Her proposal came after Local 1199 of the National Health and Service Employees Union put forward its own plan that would retrain heathcare workers who face layoffs as hospitals trim staffs to become more competitive.
New York City's plan would link its hospitals with non-profit community clinics, with the city providing funds to renovate them in return for getting a bigger share of the clinics' patients.
Gill outlined her plan during a City Council hearing. She said it had the support of District Council 37, the biggest union representing HHC workers.

Crain's New York Business has said that New York State hospitals could get as much as $1 billion over five years, a portion of the money the federal government would save if Washington grants the state's request to require all Medicaid recipients to enroll in managed care programs. This step requires the federal goverment to waive Medicaid rules.
